row_statement: Conjecture 2.8 of Burstein, Hasto and Mansour (for a set Pi of layered patterns, delta'(Pi) = delta(Pi), and among maximal Pi-containing strings in [k]^n there is one which is layered) is false through its second clause: for Pi = {11223, 13222}, n = 13 and k = 4 the word 1133422222222 has 337 occurrences while every layered word of length 13 has at most 336, so no layered word is maximal. The first clause (the density equality) is true by Barton (2004) and is not refuted.

caveats: Only the second clause of a two-part conjecture is refuted; the density equality is a theorem (Barton 2004, Theorem 3). Barton restates the second clause alone as his Conjecture 5 and names the obstruction this counterexample uses.

Not minimal: Opus found a smaller counterexample, Pi = {1243, 2113} at n = 8, k = 5 (25 against 24), not in Lean. For the pair in the Lean proof at k = 4 the failure holds at n = 13 to 17, 19 to 21 and 24 but not at 18, 22, 23 or 25 to 30.
The source reports no computation for this conjecture; a computer search finds the counterexample in about a minute.
The MathDB row's closing commentary misdescribes delta'; the displayed conjecture is verbatim. Kitaev's book and Warren's thesis were not read and remain the prior-art risk.
